questions.question: An event below the pathway with stable identifier R-HSA-168256 may be reachable by more than one route, at different depths. Counting the events it directly contains as depth 1, what is the mean shortest depth of the reaction-like events below it, rounded to four decimal places?

queries.sql: WITH RECURSIVE lv AS (SELECT he.hasEvent AS ev, 1 AS d FROM DatabaseObject o JOIN StableIdentifier s ON s.DB_ID = o.stableIdentifier JOIN Pathway_2_hasEvent he ON he.DB_ID = o.DB_ID WHERE s.identifier = 'R-HSA-168256' UNION SELECT he.hasEvent, lv.d + 1 FROM lv JOIN Pathway_2_hasEvent he ON he.DB_ID = lv.ev) SELECT ROUND(AVG(md), 4) FROM (SELECT lv.ev, MIN(lv.d) AS md FROM lv JOIN ReactionlikeEvent r ON r.DB_ID = lv.ev GROUP BY lv.ev) t;
queries.cypher:
MATCH path = (:Pathway {stId:'R-HSA-168256'})-[:hasEvent*]->(e:ReactionLikeEvent)
WITH e, min(length(path)) AS d
RETURN round(avg(d), 4)

questions.question: For each Homo sapiens pathway, count the reaction-like events anywhere beneath it, and what percentage of those have catalyst activity. Report the five pathways with the most events, ordered by highest count first, then alphabetically by pathway name. Use columns named pathway, events and pct, with pct rounded to one decimal place.

queries.sql: WITH RECURSIVE t AS (SELECT he.DB_ID AS root, he.hasEvent AS ev FROM Pathway_2_hasEvent he JOIN Event_2_species es ON es.DB_ID = he.DB_ID JOIN DatabaseObject sp ON sp.DB_ID = es.species AND sp._displayName = 'Homo sapiens' UNION SELECT t.root, he.hasEvent FROM t JOIN Pathway_2_hasEvent he ON he.DB_ID = t.ev), rle AS (SELECT DISTINCT t.root, t.ev FROM t JOIN ReactionlikeEvent r ON r.DB_ID = t.ev), agg AS (SELECT root, COUNT(*) AS n, SUM(CASE WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ReactionlikeEvent_2_catalystActivity c WHERE c.DB_ID = rle.ev) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS wc FROM rle GROUP BY root) SELECT d._displayName AS pathway, a.n AS events, ROUND(100 * a.wc / a.n, 1) AS pct FROM agg a JOIN DatabaseObject d ON d.DB_ID = a.root ORDER BY a.n DESC, pathway LIMIT 5;
queries.cypher:
MATCH (p:Pathway)-[:species]->(:Species {displayName:'Homo sapiens'})
MATCH (p)-[:hasEvent*]->(e:ReactionLikeEvent)
WITH p, count(DISTINCT e) AS events,
     count(DISTINCT CASE WHEN EXISTS { (e)-[:catalystActivity]->() } THEN e END) AS wc
RETURN p.displayName AS pathway, events, round(100.0 * wc / events, 1) AS pct
ORDER BY events DESC, pathway LIMIT 5
queries.typeql: with fun sub-events($p: event) -> { event }: match { event-containment (containing-pathway: $p, contained-event: $e); } or { event-containment (containing-pathway: $p, contained-event: $m); let $e in sub-events($m); }; return { $e }; match $p isa pathway, has display-name $pathway; species-assignment (classified-thing: $p, species: $sp); $sp has display-name "Homo sapiens"; let $e in sub-events($p); $e isa reaction-like-event; select $p, $pathway, $e; distinct; reduce $events = count($e) groupby $p, $pathway; match $events > 0; let $e in sub-events($p); $e isa reaction-like-event; catalysis (catalysed-reaction: $e, catalyst: $cat); select $p, $pathway, $events, $e; distinct; reduce $withcat = count($e) groupby $p, $pathway, $events; match let $pct = round(100.0 * $withcat / $events * 10.0) / 10.0; select $pathway, $events, $pct; sort $events desc, $pathway asc; limit 5;

questions.question: Of the Homo sapiens reaction-like events that are regulated at all, what percentage are never negatively regulated? Round to one decimal place.

queries.sql: SELECT ROUND(100 * SUM(pos_only) / COUNT(*), 1) FROM (SELECT rb.DB_ID AS ev, MAX(CASE WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ReactionlikeEvent_2_regulatedBy b JOIN NegativeRegulation nr ON nr.DB_ID = b.regulatedBy WHERE b.DB_ID = rb.DB_ID) THEN 0 ELSE 1 END) AS pos_only FROM ReactionlikeEvent_2_regulatedBy rb JOIN Event_2_species es ON es.DB_ID = rb.DB_ID JOIN DatabaseObject sp ON sp.DB_ID = es.species AND sp._displayName = 'Homo sapiens' GROUP BY rb.DB_ID) t;
queries.cypher:
MATCH (r:ReactionLikeEvent)-[:species]->(:Species {displayName:'Homo sapiens'})
WHERE EXISTS { (r)-[:regulatedBy]->() }
WITH DISTINCT r
WITH count(r) AS total,
     sum(CASE WHEN NOT EXISTS { (r)-[:regulatedBy]->(:NegativeRegulation) } THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS pos
RETURN round(100.0 * pos / total, 1)
queries.typeql: match $r isa reaction-like-event; species-assignment (classified-thing: $r, species: $sp); $sp has display-name "Homo sapiens"; regulation (regulated-event: $r, regulator: $any); select $r; distinct; reduce $total = count; match $r isa reaction-like-event; species-assignment (classified-thing: $r, species: $sp); $sp has display-name "Homo sapiens"; regulation (regulated-event: $r, regulator: $any); not { negative-regulation (regulated-event: $r, regulator: $neg); }; select $total, $r; distinct; reduce $pos = count groupby $total; match let $pct = round(100.0 * $pos / $total * 10.0) / 10.0; select $pct;

questions.question: Which people are an author of the greatest number of distinct literature references that are summations of Homo sapiens pathways? Give each person as their surname, then a comma and a space, then their first name.

queries.sql: WITH tally AS (SELECT pa.author AS person, COUNT(DISTINCT sl.literatureReference) AS n FROM Pathway pw JOIN Event_2_species es ON es.DB_ID = pw.DB_ID JOIN DatabaseObject sp ON sp.DB_ID = es.species AND sp._displayName = 'Homo sapiens' JOIN Event_2_summation s ON s.DB_ID = pw.DB_ID JOIN Summation_2_literatureReference sl ON sl.DB_ID = s.summation JOIN Publication_2_author pa ON pa.DB_ID = sl.literatureReference GROUP BY pa.author) SELECT CONCAT(pe.surname, ', ', pe.firstname) FROM tally t JOIN Person pe ON pe.DB_ID = t.person WHERE t.n = (SELECT MAX(n) FROM tally);
queries.cypher:
MATCH (p:Pathway)-[:species]->(:Species {displayName:'Homo sapiens'})
MATCH (p)-[:summation]->(:Summation)-[:literatureReference]->(lr)
MATCH (lr)<-[:author]-(person:Person)
WITH person, count(DISTINCT lr) AS n
WITH collect({person: person, n: n}) AS rows, max(n) AS top
UNWIND rows AS row
WITH row WHERE row.n = top
RETURN row.person.surname + ', ' + row.person.firstname
queries.typeql: match $p isa pathway; species-assignment (classified-thing: $p, species: $sp); $sp has display-name "Homo sapiens"; summarisation (summarised-thing: $p, summation: $s); literature-citation (citing-thing: $s, cited-publication: $lr); publication-authorship (publication: $lr, publication-author: $person); select $person, $lr; distinct; reduce $n = count($lr) groupby $person; reduce $m = max($n); match $p isa pathway; species-assignment (classified-thing: $p, species: $sp); $sp has display-name "Homo sapiens"; summarisation (summarised-thing: $p, summation: $s); literature-citation (citing-thing: $s, cited-publication: $lr); publication-authorship (publication: $lr, publication-author: $person); select $m, $person, $lr; distinct; reduce $n = count($lr) groupby $person, $m; match $n == $m; $person has surname $sn, has first-name $fn; let $name = $sn + ", " + $fn; select $name;

questions.question: Take the three species with the most reaction-like events. For each, report the pathway that directly contains the most reaction-like events of that species. Use columns species, pathway and reactions, ordered by highest count first, then alphabetically by species.

queries.sql: WITH sp3 AS (SELECT es.species AS sp, COUNT(DISTINCT es.DB_ID) AS n FROM Event_2_species es JOIN ReactionlikeEvent r ON r.DB_ID = es.DB_ID GROUP BY es.species ORDER BY n DESC LIMIT 3), cnt AS (SELECT es.species AS sp, he.DB_ID AS pw, COUNT(DISTINCT he.hasEvent) AS n FROM Pathway_2_hasEvent he JOIN ReactionlikeEvent r ON r.DB_ID = he.hasEvent JOIN Event_2_species es ON es.DB_ID = he.hasEvent WHERE es.species IN (SELECT sp FROM sp3) GROUP BY es.species, he.DB_ID), rk AS (SELECT c.sp, c.pw, c.n, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY c.sp ORDER BY c.n DESC, c.pw) AS r FROM cnt c) SELECT ds._displayName AS species, dp._displayName AS pathway, rk.n AS reactions FROM rk JOIN DatabaseObject ds ON ds.DB_ID = rk.sp JOIN DatabaseObject dp ON dp.DB_ID = rk.pw WHERE rk.r = 1 ORDER BY rk.n DESC, species;
queries.cypher:
MATCH (r:ReactionLikeEvent)-[:species]->(s:Species)
WITH s, count(DISTINCT r) AS total ORDER BY total DESC LIMIT 3
MATCH (p:Pathway)-[:hasEvent]->(e:ReactionLikeEvent)-[:species]->(s)
WITH s, p, count(DISTINCT e) AS n
ORDER BY n DESC, p.dbId
WITH s, collect({p: p, n: n})[0] AS best
RETURN s.displayName AS species, best.p.displayName AS pathway, best.n AS reactions
ORDER BY reactions DESC, species
queries.typeql: match species-assignment (classified-thing: $r, species: $s); $r isa reaction-like-event; select $s, $r; distinct; reduce $total = count($r) groupby $s; sort $total desc; limit 3; match event-containment (containing-pathway: $p, contained-event: $e); $e isa reaction-like-event; species-assignment (classified-thing: $e, species: $s); select $s, $total, $p, $e; distinct; reduce $reactions = count($e) groupby $s, $total, $p; reduce $best = max($reactions) groupby $s, $total; match event-containment (containing-pathway: $p, contained-event: $e); $e isa reaction-like-event; species-assignment (classified-thing: $e, species: $s); select $s, $total, $best, $p, $e; distinct; reduce $reactions = count($e) groupby $s, $total, $best, $p; match $reactions == $best; $s has display-name $species; $p has display-name $pathway; select $species, $pathway, $reactions; sort $reactions desc, $species asc;

questions.question: Starting from the pathway with stable identifier R-HSA-168256, consider the events it contains, directly or indirectly, and every event that directly or indirectly precedes one of those. How many reaction-like events are there?

queries.sql: WITH RECURSIVE reach AS (SELECT he.hasEvent AS ev FROM DatabaseObject o JOIN StableIdentifier s ON s.DB_ID = o.stableIdentifier JOIN Pathway_2_hasEvent he ON he.DB_ID = o.DB_ID WHERE s.identifier = 'R-HSA-168256' UNION SELECT he.hasEvent FROM reach r JOIN Pathway_2_hasEvent he ON he.DB_ID = r.ev UNION SELECT p.precedingEvent FROM reach r JOIN Event_2_precedingEvent p ON p.DB_ID = r.ev) SELECT COUNT(*) FROM reach JOIN ReactionlikeEvent x ON x.DB_ID = reach.ev;

questions.question: The pathway with stable identifier R-HSA-168256 directly contains three pathways. Compare each pair of them by the reaction-like events beneath each, reporting how many events they share and the Jaccard similarity of the two sets, rounded to four decimal places. Use columns pathway_a and pathway_b for the two names, with pathway_a the alphabetically earlier of the pair, then shared and jaccard, ordered by highest similarity first, then alphabetically by pathway_a, then pathway_b.

queries.sql: WITH RECURSIVE roots AS (SELECT he.hasEvent AS root FROM DatabaseObject o JOIN StableIdentifier s ON s.DB_ID = o.stableIdentifier JOIN Pathway_2_hasEvent he ON he.DB_ID = o.DB_ID WHERE s.identifier = 'R-HSA-168256'), tree AS (SELECT root, root AS ev FROM roots UNION SELECT t.root, he.hasEvent FROM tree t JOIN Pathway_2_hasEvent he ON he.DB_ID = t.ev), rset AS (SELECT DISTINCT t.root, t.ev FROM tree t JOIN ReactionlikeEvent r ON r.DB_ID = t.ev), sizes AS (SELECT root, COUNT(*) AS n FROM rset GROUP BY root), inter AS (SELECT a.root AS ra, b.root AS rb, COUNT(*) AS k FROM rset a JOIN rset b ON b.ev = a.ev AND b.root > a.root GROUP BY a.root, b.root) SELECT LEAST(da._displayName, db2._displayName) AS pathway_a, GREATEST(da._displayName, db2._displayName) AS pathway_b, i.k AS shared, ROUND(i.k / (sa.n + sb.n - i.k), 4) AS jaccard FROM inter i JOIN sizes sa ON sa.root = i.ra JOIN sizes sb ON sb.root = i.rb JOIN DatabaseObject da ON da.DB_ID = i.ra JOIN DatabaseObject db2 ON db2.DB_ID = i.rb ORDER BY jaccard DESC, pathway_a, pathway_b;
queries.cypher:
MATCH (:Pathway {stId:'R-HSA-168256'})-[:hasEvent]->(child)
MATCH (child)-[:hasEvent*]->(e:ReactionLikeEvent)
WITH child, collect(DISTINCT e) AS es
WITH collect({c: child, es: es}) AS rows
UNWIND rows AS a
UNWIND rows AS b
WITH a, b WHERE a.c.displayName < b.c.displayName
WITH a, b, size([x IN a.es WHERE x IN b.es]) AS shared
RETURN a.c.displayName AS pathway_a, b.c.displayName AS pathway_b, shared,
       round(1.0 * shared / (size(a.es) + size(b.es) - shared), 4) AS jaccard
ORDER BY jaccard DESC, pathway_a, pathway_b
queries.typeql: with fun sub-events($p: event) -> { event }: match { event-containment (containing-pathway: $p, contained-event: $e); } or { event-containment (containing-pathway: $p, contained-event: $m); let $e in sub-events($m); }; return { $e }; match $root isa pathway, has st-id "R-HSA-168256"; event-containment (containing-pathway: $root, contained-event: $a); event-containment (containing-pathway: $root, contained-event: $b); $a has display-name $pathway_a; $b has display-name $pathway_b; $pathway_a < $pathway_b; let $ea in sub-events($a); let $eb in sub-events($b); $ea isa reaction-like-event; $ea is $eb; select $a, $b, $pathway_a, $pathway_b, $ea; distinct; reduce $shared = count($ea) groupby $a, $b, $pathway_a, $pathway_b; match let $ea in sub-events($a); $ea isa reaction-like-event; select $a, $b, $pathway_a, $pathway_b, $shared, $ea; distinct; reduce $na = count($ea) groupby $a, $b, $pathway_a, $pathway_b, $shared; match let $eb in sub-events($b); $eb isa reaction-like-event; select $a, $b, $pathway_a, $pathway_b, $shared, $na, $eb; distinct; reduce $nb = count($eb) groupby $a, $b, $pathway_a, $pathway_b, $shared, $na; match let $jaccard = round(10000.0 * $shared / ($na + $nb - $shared)) / 10000.0; select $pathway_a, $pathway_b, $shared, $jaccard; sort $jaccard desc, $pathway_a asc, $pathway_b asc;
